purpose: The adapter registry. Adding a harness is a new module in scripts/adapters/ plus one entry here - never a core edit. A test asserts exactly that by registering a fake adapter and checking the snapshot grows, because a design that merely intends to be neutral drifts and one that is tested for it cannot.

adapters.label: Claude Code
adapters.note: Sessions from the JSONL transcripts under the Claude projects directory, tail-read. Also carries the hooks inventory, which is harness-specific, by loading build_inventory out of .claude/hooks/session-hooks-inventory.py by PATH: that filename contains hyphens, so it cannot be imported by name, and the function has exactly one caller of its own, so it was never an API.

adapters.label: GitHub Copilot Chat
adapters.note: Read-only SQLite over the VS Code extension's session store, opened file:...?mode=ro and never for writing.

documented_not_built.label: GitHub Copilot CLI
documented_not_built.reason: Those lock files carry an Authorization Nonce header and a named-pipe path. An adapter must read pid, ideName, workspaceFolders and timestamp ONLY, and must never emit the credential. Not built, so the rule is recorded rather than relied on.

documented_not_built.label: Gemini CLI
documented_not_built.reason: Not installed on the machine this was written on, so nothing could be verified against a real store.

documented_not_built.label: Codex
documented_not_built.reason: Configured through .agents/skills but never run here: the directory does not exist, so its session shape is unverified.

documented_not_built.label: opencode
documented_not_built.reason: Configuration only. No session state on disk to report, so an adapter would have nothing to add beyond the mirror matrix column that already exists.
